Cmod A7: bugs, tradeoffs and ideas to adopt

Claude’s video and audio paths pass our checks. Its no-TM1638 lab adapter needs compatibility fixes. A shared Vivado header-selection defect deserves priority in both implementations.

Claude c698aecc · Codex b9fa13b2 · Six Claude configurations compared with four Codex configurations · Review began 17 November

Recommendation: keep the current Codex board implementation as the working baseline, fix the shared production build path, then selectively adopt Claude’s wiring and clocking ideas. Preserve the demonstrated video/audio behavior while fixing the lab interface defects.

What was reviewed

Reviewed RTL, XDC, board Tcl, common lab interfaces, build include paths, English assembly instructions and supporting module schematics. Claude’s local checkout initially matched c698aecc8f87293ddfe7400f52b24257142a0c7d and the fetched remote branch. The later uncommitted README changes only append this review request; reviewed implementation files are unchanged. Codex baseline: b9fa13b2899fd2dc73290172e7776afb49364690. The retired 15T Cmod implementation is excluded.

Findings, ordered by action priority

P1: fix before relying on affected build paths. P2: bounded compatibility, reliability or documentation issue. “Reproduced” distinguishes tool evidence from unmeasured electrical risk.

8 findings shown

P1SharedReproduced

F01 · The normal Vivado include path can ignore a lab’s peripheral settings

For 3_10_spectrum_analyzer, the lab header disables TM1638 and DAC output. The production Tcl omits the lab directory from its include path. With that search order, both implementations instantiate TM1638 and the DAC; with the lab directory first, both disappear. This changes hardware selection and, in Claude’s TM1638-capable wrapper, whether onboard buttons reset the lab. The forced no-TM1638 wrappers still suppress TM1638, but the other peripheral selections remain vulnerable. Claude explicitly identified this issue in its documentation; our separate validation driver avoids it, while our documented normal build path still has it.

Evidence and source locations

Shared production Tcl, lines 49–53 · Spectrum lab header · Claude’s prior diagnosis · Paired Icarus controls for both implementations (evidence/checks.json, local file) · Vivado: production order (evidence/vivado_include_default/vivado.log, local file) · Vivado: lab first (evidence/vivado_include_lab/vivado.log, local file)

Recommended action. Fix the shared production driver to put the selected lab directory first, retain the default header as fallback, and test the actual production invocation. Compare the synthesized peripheral inventory against the selected header. This is the first change to adopt from the review.

P1ClaudeReproduced

F02 · The one-digit placeholder breaks two existing labs

All three no-TM1638 variants pass w_digit=1 into the lab. 1_08_7segment_word then requests shift_reg[0:1] from a descending vector. The FIFO exercise derives its depth from this parameter and requests valid[-1:0]. Both fail elaboration: six failures across three variants. This is a lab compatibility failure even though no physical display is attached. The same 17-lab matrix passes in all four Codex configurations.

Evidence and source locations

One-digit placeholder · Invalid shift slice · FIFO depth follows w_digit · Icarus failure (evidence/claude_cmod_a7_35_tiny_vga_640_no_tm1638_claude_1_08_7segment_word.log, local file) · Vivado independently confirms Synth 8-523 (evidence/vivado_digit/vivado.log, local file)

Recommended action. Retain a compatible internal display width, such as eight, and leave display outputs disconnected; or explicitly generalize these labs for depth/digit count one. A placeholder width of zero is also unsafe with the current lab interfaces.

P2ClaudeReproduced

F03 · The two-bit switch alias leaves the mux selector undefined

The no-TM1638 wrapper gives the lab w_key=2 and w_sw=2. The mux lab selects its switch branch whenever fewer than three keys exist, then reads sw[2]. With btn=01, all three variants produce sel=x, led=xx in simulation. Hardware synthesis may optimize the invalid bit as a don’t-care; the source does not define the intended behavior. Two physical buttons also cannot supply three independent mux inputs.

Evidence and source locations

Lab widths and switch alias · Mux input selection · Reproducer: unknown LEDs (evidence/claude_cmod_a7_35_tiny_vga_640_no_tm1638_claude_mux.log, local file)

Recommended action. Keep two keys, but expose a padded switch bus with explicitly zero unused bits, as Codex currently does, or adapt the lab to a documented two-button mapping. State the lost third independent control.

P2ClaudeStatic risk + simulation evidence

F04 · Onboard keys reach synchronous labs without a synchronizer

assign lab_key = btn connects asynchronous board inputs straight to both key and sw. A transition between clock edges immediately reaches the lab and its LED output. That is expected in a combinational lab, but clocked labs such as the binary counter consume the same raw inputs without a board-level two-stage synchronizer. This creates a metastability/reconvergence risk. Simulation proves the absence of the boundary registers; it does not reproduce analog metastability. Neither implementation provides universal mechanical debounce.

Evidence and source locations

Direct key connection · Clocked consumer · Between-edge transition probe (evidence/claude_cmod_a7_35_tiny_vga_640_no_tm1638_claude_buttons.log, local file) · AMD single-bit synchronizer guidance

Recommended action. Synchronize each onboard button through at least two destination-clock registers before providing key/sw. Keep debounce separate. Audit labs that consume these signals on a separate slow clock as an additional CDC boundary.

P2ClaudeReproduced, optional configuration

F05 · Enabling split-DIO mode breaks TM1638 elaboration

The common SPLIT_TM1638_DIO_INOUT_SIGNAL option changes the controller ports, but the three TM1638-capable wrappers always connect .sio_data(pio28). Enabling the option yields “sio_data is not a port of i_tm1638.” The ordinary unsplit LED&KEY configuration works; this is an optional-mode compatibility gap, not a default-build failure.

Evidence and source locations

Fixed controller connection · Conditional controller ports · Compile error with split DIO (evidence/claude_cmod_a7_35_claude_tiny_vga_640_split_dio.log, local file)

Recommended action. Add the conditional input/output/enable wiring and tri-state assignment, or reject this unsupported macro with a clear elaboration diagnostic. Keep an enabled-option test in CI.

P2ClaudeDocumentation defect

F06 · GY-PCM5102 needs a line-level output warning

The general instructions offer headphones or speakers for either DAC and later tell the reader to connect either. The GY section does not distinguish its output from the WeAct headphone amplifier. The PCM5102A line driver is specified for loads down to 1 kΩ, not ordinary 32 Ω headphones. The WeAct schematic includes a separate headphone amplifier, so the modules need different output-load instructions.

Evidence and source locations

Combined DAC description · GY wiring section · Common bring-up step · TI PCM510xA: line output load · WeAct V1 schematic

Recommended action. Explicitly direct the GY jack to an amplifier or active-speaker line input. Reserve direct headphone instructions for the WeAct module with its amplifier.

P2ClaudeHardware assumption, not a measured failure

F07 · The universal 3.3 V DAC supply advice needs board-specific validation

The guide feeds 3.3 V into both modules’ VCC/VIN, allows a breadboard rail as low as 3.1 V, and relies on dropout through the WeAct onboard 3.3 V regulator. TI specifies a 3.0 V minimum for the DAC’s analog/charge-pump supplies. A low input rail plus regulator drop leaves little margin; an unidentified GY clone cannot be assigned one universal VIN requirement. No loaded measurements were supplied. This does not prove either board fails at 3.3 V, and the requested 3.3 V TM1638 connection is a separate issue.

Evidence and source locations

DAC supply assumptions · Accepted rail range · TI recommended operating supplies · WeAct VCC → regulator → VDD33 path

Recommended action. Identify the exact board/regulator revision and check VDD at the DAC under load, including the low-input corner. Preserve the separately documented DAC power path until that validation exists; do not infer a module VIN range from the chip’s 3.3 V supply rating.

P2CodexConfirmed test gap

F08 · Our “controller source excluded” test filters the wrong filename

The Codex compile helper removes tm1638_board_controller.sv, but the actual module is in peripherals/tm1638_board.sv. The controller source therefore remains available. The no-TM1638 netlist checks and Vivado results still demonstrate that the controller is absent from those builds; the stronger claim that a missing source forces accidental instantiation to fail is not established by this test.

Evidence and source locations

Incorrect source filter · Actual controller source · Independent source/instance checks (evidence/checks.json, local file)

Recommended action. Filter the actual filename, assert that it is absent from the compiler input list, and add a mutation test that deliberately instantiates the excluded module. Correct the associated documentation claim until that test is fixed.

Good ideas worth adopting

These are proposals, not changes applied during this review. Each includes a check that should precede adoption.

01Adopt first

Bring the production build into the test matrix

Claude’s include-path diagnosis is the most consequential transferable idea. Fix the common driver, then validate enabled peripherals from actual lab headers, rather than relying only on a separate build driver.

Gate: spectrum analyzer omits TM1638/DAC in both header selection and synthesized hierarchy.

02Adopt with compatibility checks

Add VGA parameter validation

Validate positive clock values, integer clock/pixel ratios and the four-bit divider’s supported ratio (1–16). Claude already proposes most of this check. Add the zero-frequency cases before division/modulo and exercise the assertion mechanism in supported synthesis tools.

Gate: invalid configurations fail clearly; every supported tool accepts the check. Claude’s proposed guard

03Offer as a wiring option

Expose Pmod power through a pass-through breakout

Claude’s Pmod TPH2 option gives access to JA power and signals while TinyVGA stays connected. This is useful for the microphone and a characterized TM1638 load. Preserve a current budget for the board rail, check connector orientation, and keep DAC supply selection board-specific.

Gate: measured loaded rail, total current budget, mechanical cable support. Digilent TPH2

04Prototype and benchmark

Consider a 50 MHz system-clock option

Claude generates 50 MHz from a 750 MHz MMCM VCO. Its video remains 25 MHz and its audio rates match our 100 MHz mode. Our independent graphics build passes. This provides more clock-period margin for that design, but does not establish a measured power reduction or prove that all labs should run at 50 MHz.

Gate: broader lab timing/performance comparison, UART/timebase audit, power measurement if power is the goal.

05Offer alongside existing timing

Evaluate the 304-column no-PLL mode

Claude’s 381-clock line puts frame timing closer to nominal 640×480/59.94 Hz. Our 382-clock, 305-column mode matches active-line duration more closely. Keep these as measurable tradeoffs; test actual monitors before changing the default.

Gate: monitor acceptance, image centering, geometry and text readability. The timing comparison below quantifies both.

06Adopt in a separate wiring revision

Group pins by module header order

Claude puts DAC BCK/DIN/WS on DIP 21–23 next to VU, and GND/STB/CLK/DIO on DIP 25–28 in TM1638 header order. That can reduce wire crossings. It is electrically incompatible with our current accessory pin map, so changing it requires an explicit rewiring/version transition.

Gate: diagram/table/RTL agreement and continuity check. Do not silently reuse our current bitstream with Claude wiring.

07Adopt selectively

Document verified onboard pulls and module-specific drawings

The WeAct V1 schematic shows an MCLK pull-down (R17) and the shutdown pull-up. Claude correctly allows MC and /SD to remain open on that exact revision. Our explicit MCLK-to-GND wire is conservative, not a bug. Separate DAC/power diagrams are useful, but use shared generators rather than copied full guides for every clock variant.

Gate: verify the actual PCB revision; preserve an explicit ground instruction for modules without the pull-down.

The no-PLL timing tradeoff

Calculated from the configured pixel rates and raster totals; all modes use 525 lines. The reference row uses conventional 25.175 MHz, 800×525 timing. Rounded figures do not certify monitor compatibility.

ModeActive columnsClocks / lineLine durationActive durationFrame rate
Nominal reference64080031.7776 µs25.4220 µs59.940476 Hz
Claude 640 / Codex 64064080032.0000 µs25.6000 µs59.523810 Hz
Claude 30430438131.7500 µs25.3333 µs59.992501 Hz
Codex 30530538231.8333 µs25.4167 µs59.835453 Hz
Claude 32032040033.3333 µs26.6667 µs57.142857 Hz

304 columns give a frame rate closer to 59.94 Hz; 305 columns give an active duration closer to the reference. The 320-column mode deliberately trades timing for a convenient horizontal sample count, producing 30 kHz lines and 57.143 Hz frames. Claude documents the monitor-acceptance risk. It should remain an experimental option, not be reported as a broken implementation merely for using nonstandard timing. Exact LCD sampling and pixel width depend on the monitor.

Sources: Claude 304 timing · Claude 320 timing · Codex 305 timing.

Checks performed and their limits

Supporting evidence, source snapshots, reproduction scripts and previews are stored locally at /home/verilog/codex/cmod_a7/competitive_review_20261118/, outside the repository. File names below are relative to that directory and are not downloadable attachments. Only the English and Russian HTML reports and README.md are included in the repository.

  • Compilation: Claude 96/102; Codex 68/68. The six Claude failures share the one-digit placeholder root cause. Mux undefined behavior requires simulation and is not included in the compile-failure count.
  • Targeted controls: no-TM1638 mux values, between-edge button propagation, split-DIO compilation, and lab-first versus production-order includes. Structured results (evidence/checks.json, local file).
  • Video and audio: all six Claude variants passed full raster totals, sync positions/polarity, active coordinates, blanking, RGB pin order, a 24-bit INMP441 sample, stereo I²S word alignment and microphone/DAC clock-period checks. Simulation results (evidence/video_audio.json, local file).
  • Independent Vivado build: Claude’s 50 MHz rectangle/ellipse/parabola example completed synthesis, placement, routing and bitstream generation: WNS +14.657 ns, WHS +0.061 ns, 203 LUTs, 110 registers, one MMCM and one BUFG. Build log (evidence/vivado_640_graphics/vivado.log, local file) · Timing report (evidence/vivado_640_graphics/timing_summary.rpt, local file) · Utilization (evidence/vivado_640_graphics/utilization.rpt, local file).
  • Vivado failure control: the no-TM1638 640 configuration with the seven-segment word lab fails at the same invalid slice as Icarus. Header-order control logs are identified in F01.

The successful graphics build has zero DRC errors; CFGBVS-1 and graphics DSP pipelining warnings remain. External I/O delays are unspecified in the preserved master XDC. Clock models are behavioral, with no analog lock or metastability model. No board was programmed. No real monitor, audio load or power rail was tested. This review independently routed the Claude 640 mode; the 304/320 modes were simulated and elaborated, not newly routed here.

Our previously recorded comparable 100 MHz graphics build used 206 LUTs and 115 registers with +5.220 ns setup slack. The clock period differs, so raw slack does not rank achievable frequency or total quality. No power claim follows from these figures. Earlier Codex build record (evidence/prior_codex_vivado_results.json, local file).

Local reproduction scripts: Lab/constraint/option checks (run_checks.py, local file) · Video/audio checks (check_video_audio.py, local file) · Vivado driver (review_vivado.tcl, local file) · Pinned source hashes (evidence/source_manifest.json, local file).

Recommended action plan

  1. Fix shared header selection and validate the production path. This benefits both implementations and prevents misleading peripheral builds.
  2. Repair Claude’s no-TM1638 lab adapter. Safe internal digit width, padded switch inputs, synchronized keys; rerun the 17-lab matrix and targeted mux probes.
  3. Close smaller gaps. Split-DIO support or explicit rejection, DAC load/power wording, and our incorrect controller-source exclusion test.
  4. Prototype the useful alternatives. TPH2 power access and 50 MHz / 304-column options, followed by measured hardware trials. Keep pin-map changes separately versioned.

No implementation fixes or hardware programming were performed for this review. The user subsequently authorized committing and pushing these reports; the implementation recommendations remain proposals. Only the English and Russian HTML reports and README.md are included in misc/ai_sessions/20261118_cmod_a7_support/codex. The report preserves the related prompts; supporting files and the prompt-history working copy remain in the local review directory outside the repository.

Later implementation update: full GPIO bus

On 21 November 2026 the Codex Cmod A7 implementation was expanded to expose all 44 digital DIP GPIOs as inout to lab_top in all four configurations. With microphone, DAC and TM1638 enabled, DIP 1–14, 17–23 and 35–48 are free (35 pins); without TM1638, DIP 26–28 are also free (38 pins). Disabled accessory interfaces release their GPIO drivers. See the current mapping and current validation. The findings and measurements above describe the recorded review commits and remain historical; they have not been relabelled as results for this update.
